summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of systolic heart failure (LVEF 20%), ischemic cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and obesity, was admitted after presenting with eye swelling and a hand rash, but found to have worsening shortness of breath and volume overload. Evaluation revealed mild pulmonary edema on chest X-ray and elevated proBNP, consistent with acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbation. He was treated with a furosemide IV drip, resulting in good urine output and symptom improvement. Due to a personal commitment to attend a close friend's funeral, he was discharged earlier than ideal after receiving metolazone to accelerate diuresis. His weight decreased from 134.3 kg to 131.6 kg, though still above his dry weight of 128.7 kg. The hand rash and pruritus, likely related to chronic eosinophilia and dry skin, improved with hydroxyzine. He was discharged home on his full regimen, including torsemide 140 mg daily, with instructions to monitor weight and follow up closely.
